zotero.abstractNote: Grokking, the phenomenon where neural networks generalize long after achieving zero training error, remains a central mystery in deep learning. We provide a theoretical framework to explain grokking in transformers by analyzing the interplay between the model's inductive bias and the data distribution. We show that grokking can be understood as a phase transition in the optimization landscape, driven by the competition between different components of the model's inductive bias. Our results provide a rigorous foundation for understanding the emergence of generalization in transformers and suggest new strategies for improving their performance.
